## Measurement spec

`spec:A10`

| field | value |
|---|---|
| collector | lighthouse |
| collector_pin | lighthouse-cli>=12 |
| evidence_kind | status codes + raw HTML + rendered DOM |
| indicator_code | A10 |
| instrument_entry | assessment/instrument/RULE-A10-v3.yaml |
| instrument_state | project_defined |
| leg | A10 |
| mode | auto |
| prior_art | internal draft: FSS Machine Diagnostic spec (operator-held) |
| rf_fail | One of three things, named in the result: a made-up address came back as a normal "OK" page instead of an error (which may be a platform or vendor default rather than the agency's choice); the direct link itself came back as an error; or fewer than two thousand characters of text were present before scripts ran. It is not a claim that the tool is unusable in a browser or by a crawler that runs JavaScript, nor a finding about the agency's intent. |
| rf_fix_line | Return a real status for routes that do not exist. |
| rf_hypothesis | Does the agency's interactive data tool answer a machine client honestly: real content at a deep link, and a real error for a route that does not exist? An SI client that receives HTTP 200 with an error page, or an empty shell that needs a browser to fill, records a page that is not there or reads nothing. |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not look at one or more pages, for one of three reasons: the host refused the identified client; the client's own robots.txt compliance kept it from reading the page; or it could not confirm an absence, or a server or network error stopped it. |
| rf_partial | Some of the agency's data pages that were looked at met this and some did not. |
| rf_pass | The direct link came back as a working page carrying at least two thousand characters of text before any script ran, and the made-up address correctly came back as an error rather than a normal "OK" page. |
| rf_plain_name | Data tool answers with real status and content |
| rf_question | Does the agency's interactive data tool answer a machine honestly — real content at a direct link, and a real "not found" error for a web address that does not exist? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.txt", "quote": "indicates that the origin server did not find a current representation for the target resource"}, {"source": "https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes", "quote": "Search Console will show a soft 404 error"}, {"source": "https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics", "quote": "Googlebot queues all pages with a 200 HTTP status code for rendering"}] |
| rf_rung_two_changes | Nothing: this check needs no key. |
| rf_standards_urls | https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.txt; https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes; https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics |
| rf_state | project_defined |
| rf_what_client_does | The public client asks for the tool's direct link, then asks for a made-up address under the same tool that should not exist, and reads what each answer returns. |
| rf_where_we_look | At the one interactive data tool the agency offers, looked at from the site level: its direct link to a product, and a made-up address beneath that tool. |
| rf_who_else | No public tool runs this exact check. |
| rf_why_it_matters | An RFC defines what a real "not found" answer is, and Google's crawler documentation treats an "OK" page that is really an error as a problem, not a page; a Data on the Web Best Practice expects programmatic access to return the responses a client expects. The rule that at least two thousand characters be present before scripts run is the project's own choice. |
| rule_id | RULE-A10-v3 |
| signal | For an interactive data tool: request a deep link and an invalid route; compare status codes and pre-JS HTML; a soft-404 is HTTP 200 with an error shell. Render once to compare pre- and post-JS DOM. |

## Evidence

| doc_id | doc_type | title | locator (evidence cell) |
|---|---|---|---|
| w3c-dwbp-2017 | standard | Data on the Web Best Practices (W3C Recommendation, 31 January 2017) | BP 9, persistent URIs as identifiers of datasets: "developers may build URIs into their code and so it is important that those URIs persist and that they dereference to the same resource over time"; and BP 27, preserve identifiers: a dereference that leads to "the infamous 404" must tell the client whether the absence is permanent or temporary, which is the property a soft-404 destroys |
| wilkinson-2016-fair-guiding-principles | academic | The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship | F1: globally unique and persistent identifier; A2: metadata accessible even when the data are no longer available |
